events.summary:
The second release from Suicide Basin is ongoing. Based on an
observed earlier start time of water draining from the basin, the
crest time for the Mendenhall Lake and River has been adjusted to
early Friday morning. Minor to moderate flooding continues to be
expected near Mendenhall Lake and River Thursday night into Friday
morning.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 745 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent or occurring. Water levels will,
continue to rise and water temperatures will fall within the lake,
and river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 920 PM AKDT, gauge data reported a glacier-dammed lake
outburst. Flooding is expected to begin shortly, especially near
The Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 8:30pm the stage was 7.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.8 to 10.3 feet is expected between 5
to 9am Friday. Water levels will go above minor flood stage of 9
feet around 2am Friday. Water levels will reach moderate flood
stage of 10 feet around 5 to 9am Friday. Water levels will fall
below minor flood stage late morning Friday.

Impacts:
At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.
At 9.0 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.
At 9.5 feet: Water levels up to 0.5 feet will cover Skaters Cabin
Road between Skaters Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead. Campsite 7
will be flooded with water starting to flow over the road between
campsites 8 and 9 in the Mendenhall Campground.
At 10.0 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with
up to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN SLOWLY MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST AND INCHING
CLOSER TO ALAMAGAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Saipan, Tinian and
their adjacent coastal waters, as well as Alamagan, Pagan, and
Agrihan in the CNMI. A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan,
Pagan, and Agrihan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please listen
closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect for
your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 1 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was
located near latitude 17.2N and longitude 144.7E. This was about 260
miles north of Guam. Choi-wan is moving west-northwest at 5 mph, slowing
down before pivoting toward the north-northeast with little change
in forward speed through Saturday as it moves up the Far Northern
Marianas. Maximum sustained winds have increased to 65 mph. Choi-wan
is forecast to intensify through tonight, possibly becoming a
typhoon later today. Tropical storm force winds continue to extend
outward from the center up to 125 miles, however, the wind field is
expected to expand farther south over the next few hours.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-wan continues to move away from Anatahan and is
inching closer to Alamagan, pivoting slowly to the north-northeast
through Saturday. During this time, the wind field will continue to
expand, exposing Tinian and Saipan in Tropical Storm condition a
little longer, now through Saturday. While showers have tapered a
little earlier in the day, rainbands that pummeled Guam and Rota
earlier this morning are now being pulled toward Tinian and Saipan,
with more intense showers and thunderstorms expected tonight.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor flooding along the West Fork Big Blue River in
portions of York and Fillmore counties continue.

* WHERE...Southeastern York County in east central Nebraska...
Northwestern Fillmore County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations continues.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1136 PM CDT, automated river gauges continue to indicate
ongoing minor flooding along the West Fork Big Blue River, as a
result of heavy rainfall over the last few days. As of 11:00PM
CDT, an automated gauge north of Grafton reported a stage of
13.3,  which was 2.3 feet above the minor flood stage of 11.0
feet. Given the recent trends indicating a substantial slowdown
of increasing water levels, we suspect that the water levels may
be soon to crest tonight. It is likely that water levels along
the West Fork Big Blue River will remain in minor flood stage
until at least sometime Friday or Friday night before dropping
back below flood stage.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Fork Big Blue River, Turkey Creek, Little Sandy Creek,
Beaver Creek, Big Sandy Creek, Pawnee Creek, School Creek, Sleepy
Hollow Creek, Scott Creek, Buffalo Creek, Johnson Creek, Walnut
Creek, South Fork Turkey Creek, Galaway Creek, Stone Creek, Dry
Sandy Creek, Dove Creek, Little Blue River, Thirtytwo Mile Creek,
Dry Run Creek, Liberty Creek and Oak Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction, and rural areas along the West Fork Big Blue
River both upstream and downstream of McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
